promises.promise: Shows what is ready to pick up, most urgent first.
Lets a person or an agent claim work, comment on it and close it.
Groups work under a parent and holds back what is blocked.
Carries a question to a person when the work needs a decision.
Every task has an owner. Its project, or else its owner, decides who sees it.
A task names the conversation it came from.
The question also appears in that person's Inbox.
Other tasks. One parent at most, any number of blockers.
A pull request that mentions the task is linked to it.
A task is ready when it is open, is not an epic and nothing blocks it. Claiming it moves it to in progress. Closing it takes a reason, and the reason cancelled marks it cancelled.
A task sits under one parent at most. An epic groups other tasks and is never ready itself. A blocked task waits until the task blocking it closes.
People and agents leave comments as work moves. Loom keeps them in order, oldest first, each with who wrote it and when.
A task can carry one question, with what happens on yes and on no. The person answers yes or no, or in words. The question also appears in that person's Inbox.
a Every task has an owner. A member, an agent or the household. There is no task without one.
b Who sees it. Its project's people when it has a project. Otherwise its owner, and for an agent's task, that agent's owners. Household owners always.
c Checked at the door. Loom applies this to callers from outside: a person, an agent, a machine, someone's own program. Loom's own parts read tasks without asking.
Status, priority, project, owner and assignee are columns, so the ready queue, a project's task list and a person's assignments are each one query.
Ready work is listed in the Tasks tile.
A task detail displays its title, goal, reason and owner.
The task detail offers claim, close and comment.
